population.span: In a double-blind, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned critically ill patients to receive BMES (Plasma-Lyte 148) or saline as fluid therapy in the intensive care unit (ICU) for 90 days.

endpoint.span: The primary outcome was death from any cause within 90 days after randomization.

estimate.span: Death within 90 days after randomization occurred in 530 of 2433 patients (21.8%) in the BMES group and in 530 of 2413 patients (22.0%) in the saline group, for a difference of -0.15 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -3.60 to 3.30; P = 0.90).

ci.span: Death within 90 days after randomization occurred in 530 of 2433 patients (21.8%) in the BMES group and in 530 of 2413 patients (22.0%) in the saline group, for a difference of -0.15 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -3.60 to 3.30; P = 0.90).

treatment_strategy.span: In a double-blind, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned critically ill patients to receive BMES (Plasma-Lyte 148) or saline as fluid therapy in the intensive care unit (ICU) for 90 days.

follow_up.span: The primary outcome was death from any cause within 90 days after randomization.

absent_reason.analysis_set: No held source explicitly identifies the analysis population for the mortality estimate as ITT, mITT, per-protocol, or all randomised.

served_mismatch: The served arm-level mortality counts match the abstract. However, served_outcome.served_estimand is HR, whereas the reported estimate and confidence interval are a risk difference in percentage points; neither an HR nor an RR is reported. The served_row intention-to-treat label is not stated in the held sources.

entry_population_matches_question.why: The trial enrolled critically ill ICU patients, with patients younger than 18 excluded; the requested ITT analysis set remains unverified.
entry_population_matches_question.span: Exclusion Criteria: * Age less than 18 years

notes: Endpoint, counts, risk difference and confidence interval are bound to the abstract. The registry supports the adult age restriction. The reported confidence interval applies to RD, not RR or HR; no effect measure was calculated.
